item.research_question: Can a low-temperature, rapid single-source precursor approach be used to synthesize a phase-pure, high-entropy 2D hexernary transition metal dichalcogenide (MoWReMnCr)S2 that exhibits enhanced hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity compared to 2H-MoS2?
item.material_system: Hexernary high-entropy metal disulfide (MoWReMnCr)S2; 2H-MoS2 (control); 20% w/w carbon black (CB) composite
item.processing_route: Tandem thermal decomposition of five equimolar metal dithiocarbamate precursors (MoL4, WS(S2)L2, Re2(µ–S)2(L)4, MnL3, CrL3) at 500 °C for 1 h under argon flow (300 cm3 min−1); followed by liquid-phase exfoliation (LPE) in N-methyl pyrrolidine for 24 h with ultrasonication (37 kHz, 30% power) and centrifugation (1500 rpm, 3 h)
item.test_conditions: HER electrocatalysis in 0.5 M H2SO4 electrolyte; Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) at 5 mV s−1; Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) at −0.47 V vs Ag/AgCl; Chronopotentiometry at 10 mA cm−2 for 20 h; 7000-cycle CV stability test
key_findings: The synthesized (MoWReMnCr)S2 contains 5.0 mol% Mn and 4.7 mol% Cr successfully incorporated into the 2H-MoS2 lattice, confirmed by pXRD and Raman spectroscopy.
Exfoliated nanosheets consist of 3–7 atomic layers with a homogeneous elemental distribution at the nanoscale, verified by HAADF-STEM and EDX mapping.
The (MoWReMnCr)S2@20%CB electrode achieved an overpotential of 229 ± 5 mV to reach 10 mA cm−2, significantly lower than the 362 mV for MoS2@20%CB.
The onset potential for (MoWReMnCr)S2@20%CB was −127 mV, compared to −219 mV for MoS2@20%CB.
The Tafel slope for (MoWReMnCr)S2 was 133.8 mV dec−1, indicating a Volmer-limited mechanism, compared to 152.9 mV dec−1 for MoS2.
Charge transfer resistance (Rct) for (MoWReMnCr)S2@20%CB was 3.12 Ω cm2, approximately eight times lower than the 25.11 Ω cm2 for MoS2@20%CB.
DFT calculations predicted that Cr and Mn substitutions activate the basal plane, reducing H adsorption energy (Eads) to near the optimal value of −0.24 eV.
The catalyst demonstrated high stability, retaining activity after 7000 CV cycles and 20 h of continuous operation at 10 mA cm−2.
item.mechanism: The enhanced catalytic activity is attributed to the 'cocktail effect' where the high configurational entropy stabilizes the 2H phase and allows for the incorporation of Cr and Mn. DFT calculations suggest that substituting Mo with Cr and Mn activates the basal plane sites toward H adsorption, shifting the reaction mechanism to a Volmer-limited process with near-thermoneutral H adsorption energetics, while largely preserving the favorable electronic structure of MoS2.
item.limitations: The study notes that the exfoliation process produced a size dispersion of nanosheets, and while purification to isolate monolayers is possible via liquid cascade centrifugation, it was beyond the scope of the current work. Additionally, the calculated electrochemically-active surface area (ECSA) using double-layer capacitance was deemed unreliable due to high frequency dispersion effects, requiring an alternative strategy using cyclic voltammetry.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the scalable synthesis approach is a universal route to produce 2D high-entropy materials of various transition-metal disulfides and that entropic stabilization of nanosheets is a powerful approach to produce 2D materials that cannot otherwise be produced due to intrinsic instability in the low-dimensional limit.
quotes: A low‐temperature (500 °C) and rapid (1 h) single source precursor approach is successfully adopted to synthesize the hexernary high‐entropy metal disulfide (MoWReMnCr)S2.

Substitution with the first‐row transition metals (TMs) Cr and Mn in particular produces a large activation, and some of the models incorporating these elements are predicted to have binding sites with E ads close to the −0.24 eV required for optimal H adsorption and release kinetics.

Question: Can a low-temperature, rapid single-source precursor approach be used to synthesize a phase-pure, high-entropy 2D hexernary transition metal dichalcogenide (MoWReMnCr)S2 that exhibits enhanced hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity compared to 2H-MoS2?. System: Hexernary high-entropy metal disulfide (MoWReMnCr)S2; 2H-MoS2 (control); 20% w/w carbon black (CB) composite. Processing: Tandem thermal decomposition of five equimolar metal dithiocarbamate precursors (MoL4, WS(S2)L2, Re2(µ–S)2(L)4, MnL3, CrL3) at 500 °C for 1 h under argon flow (300 cm3 min−1); followed by liquid-phase exfoliation (LPE) in N-methyl pyrrolidine for 24 h with ultrasonication (37 kHz, 30% power) and centrifugation (1500 rpm, 3 h). Test conditions: HER electrocatalysis in 0.5 M H2SO4 electrolyte; Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) at 5 mV s−1; Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) at −0.47 V vs Ag/AgCl; Chronopotentiometry at 10 mA cm−2 for 20 h; 7000-cycle CV stability test. Findings: The synthesized (MoWReMnCr)S2 contains 5.0 mol% Mn and 4.7 mol% Cr successfully incorporated into the 2H-MoS2 lattice, confirmed by pXRD and Raman spectroscopy.; Exfoliated nanosheets consist of 3–7 atomic layers with a homogeneous elemental distribution at the nanoscale, verified by HAADF-STEM and EDX mapping.; The (MoWReMnCr)S2@20%CB electrode achieved an overpotential of 229 ± 5 mV to reach 10 mA cm−2, significantly lower than the 362 mV for MoS2@20%CB.; The onset potential for (MoWReMnCr)S2@20%CB was −127 mV, compared to −219 mV for MoS2@20%CB.; The Tafel slope for (MoWReMnCr)S2 was 133.8 mV dec−1, indicating a Volmer-limited mechanism, compared to 152.9 mV dec−1 for MoS2.; Charge transfer resistance (Rct) for (MoWReMnCr)S2@20%CB was 3.12 Ω cm2, approximately eight times lower than the 25.11 Ω cm2 for MoS2@20%CB.; DFT calculations predicted that Cr and Mn substitutions activate the basal plane, reducing H adsorption energy (Eads) to near the optimal value of −0.24 eV.; The catalyst demonstrated high stability, retaining activity after 7000 CV cycles and 20 h of continuous operation at 10 mA cm−2.. Mechanism: The enhanced catalytic activity is attributed to the 'cocktail effect' where the high configurational entropy stabilizes the 2H phase and allows for the incorporation of Cr and Mn. DFT calculations suggest that substituting Mo with Cr and Mn activates the basal plane sites toward H adsorption, shifting the reaction mechanism to a Volmer-limited process with near-thermoneutral H adsorption energetics, while largely preserving the favorable electronic structure of MoS2.. Limitations: The study notes that the exfoliation process produced a size dispersion of nanosheets, and while purification to isolate monolayers is possible via liquid cascade centrifugation, it was beyond the scope of the current work. Additionally, the calculated electrochemically-active surface area (ECSA) using double-layer capacitance was deemed unreliable due to high frequency dispersion effects, requiring an alternative strategy using cyclic voltammetry.. Future work: The authors propose that the scalable synthesis approach is a universal route to produce 2D high-entropy materials of various transition-metal disulfides and that entropic stabilization of nanosheets is a powerful approach to produce 2D materials that cannot otherwise be produced due to intrinsic instability in the low-dimensional limit..
